fact: Until 1 January 1920 Gestel was part of the municipality Gestel en Blaarthem; then it merged into Eindhoven together with Stratum, Strijp, Tongelre and Woensel.
The Genneper watermill is first mentioned in a 13th-century document, when it was donated to Postel Abbey in Mol, Belgium.
The Genneper watermill burned down and was rebuilt in 1587.
The mill was a banmolen: local farmers were obliged to have their grain ground there.
Vincent van Gogh painted the Genneper watermill four times in 1884.
The mill has been a rijksmonument (national monument number 14639) since 15 August 1972.
In 1866 Gestel got a small station on the railway line from Eindhoven to Valkenswaard and Hasselt; the building still stands on the Hoogstraat.
The Sint-Lambertuskerk on the Hoogstraat was built in 1911 by architect Wolter te Riele.
In 1972 Bishop Bluyssen ordered the Sint-Lambertuskerk to be demolished; parish protests, including a two-month occupation, stopped it, and the church later became a rijksmonument.
The statue of Saint George and the dragon in front of the church was unveiled on 10 May 1931 for the 500th anniversary of the Sint-Jorisgilde of Gestel and Blaarthem.
The High Tech Campus began as a business area in 1998; it calls itself the smartest square kilometre in Europe.
Cafe De Gouden Bal claims to be the oldest pub in Eindhoven.
